summary: GPU-resident speculative round: draft, verify, device accept and frontier advance in two CUDA graphs with one readback, for greedy requests and for sampled requests verified by rejection sampling
implementation_scope: CUDA reference greedy-accept and truncation kernels, a single-row C++20 round controller over Core CudaBackend with Forward/Finish graph capture, one readback_async per round and stage timing, a C++/Python round/step budget, and a composed toy (synthetic attention plus gated-delta target, bigram drafter) through a real Core Engine. Sampled requests reuse the accept kernel on predictions from token-sampling's enqueue_verify (the target's own draws for greedy drafts, rejection sampling for sampled drafts, Core's counter-based draws), with a sampled-round fixture through both kernels. Engine draft, verify and state steps are supplied callables; no tuned or model-specific kernels.

agent_guidance.use_when: A synchronous speculative loop is correct but host round trips, per-token readbacks or host acceptance dominate the round, for greedy or sampled requests
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Verifying K+1 columns costs about K+1 ordinary steps, or the engine cannot keep per-column state for prefix selection; or routed experts stream from host memory, where every verify column adds its own expert misses
provides: Sampled rounds: the same accept kernel on rejection-sampling predictions from token-sampling, with the history commit as the first Forward kernel
Device greedy acceptance matching GreedySpeculator: prefix match, correction or bonus, allowance bound and stop handling
Device-resident control block with frontier advance by n_emitted and pending-token update, without host writes during decoding
Device truncation for a smaller Core-accepted count, rerunning engine state selection
Forward and Finish CUDA graph capture of engine steps with an eager mode for comparison
Exactly one readback_async of the packed {n_emitted, tokens[K+1]} result per round and Forward/Finish stage timings
RoundBudget tokens per round, round/step ratio, implied speedup and pass/fail at a default 1.3 threshold
Fixed-width catch-up plan for stateful drafters, so the draft step's launch shape never depends on the device-held emitted count
A host check that a batched operator computes every column bitwise identically at any batch width, with fixed-order and width-dependent reference operators
engine_supplies: Capture-safe draft, verify and commit_state device steps for the actual model
Per-column provisional state (KV columns, recurrent checkpoints or saved inputs) sufficient to select any accepted prefix
Prefill, Core Session adapter and resource reservations for per-column state
Ordinary-step timing baseline and the decision to keep speculation from measured round cost
preserve: Acceptance stays on the device and uses the greedy prefix/correction/stop rule over argmax (greedy) or rejection-sampling (sampled) predictions
One device-to-host copy per round and no host fence inside launch
Frontier advances by n_emitted and the accepted state is verify column n_emitted minus one
A Core truncation is applied to device state before the next round
commit_state is idempotent from round-start state
A stateful drafter writes each position before reading it, so fixed-width catch-up junk is overwritten before any read
Verify and step kernels compute each column identically for any number of columns (fixed K split and reduction order)
adapt: Drafter, draft width and per-configuration graph slots; sweep the width on mixed text (prose, code, reasoning, another language) rather than one prompt, or choose it per round from recent acceptance
Drafter cost: a draft-only weight copy in a cheaper encoding or a draft vocabulary subset changes acceptance only, so it lets a wider draft pay
Provisional state strategy: checkpoints versus recomputation from saved inputs
Batching rows through the multi-row accept kernel and fusing accept into the verify epilogue

requires.hardware: CUDA 13.1+ GPU through Core CRIT_CORE_CUDA, CMake 3.28+ with CUDA C++20; Python 3.11+ for the budget reference
requires.model: Greedy target with capture-safe draft and K+1-column verify steps and selectable per-column state
requires.workload: Single-row greedy speculative decoding with a fixed draft width per captured configuration

contract.input: Core CudaBackend, draft width, vocabulary, context capacity, stop IDs and engine draft/verify/commit_state steps; per round a positive output allowance
contract.output: Per round the device-chosen tokens (1..K+1), a readiness event, Forward/Finish DeviceTiming values and an advanced device frontier
contract.ownership: The controller owns control, draft, prediction and result buffers, pinned result/allowance buffers, the completion event, the stage timer and graphs; steps own their model state. Borrowed tokens expire at commit or the next launch. Serialize access
contract.failure: Reject missing steps, out-of-vocabulary stops, rounds past context, launches before start or with a pending round, invalid device counts or tokens and over-long commits. A failed truncation leaves device state undefined and the request must fail. Destruction drains the stream and retains graphs if draining fails
contract.core_boundary: Session.advance launches one round and returns its readback event as readiness with deferred_tokens; Session.ready_tokens returns the device-chosen tokens after Core's single wait; device_timings returns the stage timings; Session.commit applies the accepted count; Session.close abandons a round Core cancelled after launch

validation.host: Python and C++ RoundBudget ratio, speedup and threshold checks; fixed-width drafter catch-up equal to exact variable-width ingestion over 120 randomized rounds (draft widths 1, 3, 5); column-invariance check: a fixed summation order passes and a width-dependent split is detected
validation.native: CUDA accept kernel against host GreedySpeculator on 4000 randomized rows (K 1..4, all-match, first mismatch, stop, output budget, zero budget) with frontier and truncation checks; synthetic hash-chain target for graph replay versus eager, ordinary-greedy equality for K 0..4, truncated continuation and one device-to-host copy per round counted at the CUDA API; composed toy through Core Engine matching ordinary greedy output for two prompts, graph and eager mode and K 0, one readback and one Forward/Finish trace event pair per round, and request-stop truncation; per-request device stop replacement and abandon() of a launched round left uncommitted by cancellation; sampled rounds: verify predictions through the accept and commit kernels equal a host round over Core's laws and draws (the target's draw per column, drafts kept while they match), K 0 equals one ordinary draw, and positions and counts follow the emitted and truncated counts
validation.performance: No speed claim; the reference kernels are not tuned and RoundBudget measures each engine's own round. The toy prints its round/step ratio, which typically fails 1.3 because its attention reference processes verify columns serially
